summary: Phase B (BGE/Qwen reranker re-enable) needs ONLY a docstring/comment refresh in chains.py — RERANKER_BACKEND=qwen is already in .env, and the call path is sync (search_hotel_knowledge is a sync @tool in src/agent/hotel_tools.py:847 invoked via LangChain's tool executor, which runs sync tools in a thread pool). No asyncio.to_thread wrapper is needed; document_search itself is sync (chains.py:301 `def`, not `async def`), and the CrossEncoder.compress_documents call already runs off the FastAPI event loop. The original 'event-loop blocking' note in the docstring is stale. Phase C replaces _get_text_splitter() with a two-stage MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter (H1/H2/H3) -> RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter fallback, and prepends a `Hotel > {h1} > {h2} > {h3}:\n` breadcrumb to each chunk's page_content BEFORE the vectorstore.add_documents() call. All 10 hotel markdown files have a consistent H1 (doc title) + H2 (section) structure; spa_wellness.md adds H3, and the splitter handles it gracefully. The breadcrumb is injected via a new _split_markdown_with_breadcrumbs() helper called from both ingest_docs() and ingest_text(). Both changes land in src/retrievers/hotel_knowledge/chains.py; scripts/ingest_hotel_knowledge.py is unchanged (still calls retriever.ingest_docs per file and clear_collection() at the top, which conveniently wipes the 49 stale chunks). Expected backtest delta is +6 to +9 pp on the strategic eval set (Phase C contributes most via header-context disambiguation of policy/dining queries; Phase B adds ~+2 pp Top-1 precision via cross-encoder reranking of top-30 -> top-5).

files_touched.why: Phase B: refresh stale 'reranker is OFF by default' docstring and flip the RERANKER_BACKEND default literal from 'none' to 'qwen' so the code default matches the new .env value (defence-in-depth if .env is ever missing). The event-loop-blocking concern doesn't apply: document_search is sync and called via LangChain's sync @tool path, which runs in a worker thread. Phase C: replace the single RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with a two-stage Markdown-aware pipeline (MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter on H1/H2/H3, then RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter fallback for chunks still >CHUNK_SIZE), and prepend `Hotel > {h1} > {h2} > {h3}:\n{content}` breadcrumbs in both ingest_docs() and ingest_text() so the embedding model sees the section context. Also stores breadcrumb/h1/h2/h3 in chunk metadata for debugging and future filter support.

+    def _split_markdown_with_breadcrumbs(
+        self, text: str, source: str
+    ) -> List[Document]:
+        """Split markdown on H1/H2/H3 headers, fall back to the character
+        splitter for chunks still >CHUNK_SIZE, and prepend a
+        `Hotel > {h1} > {h2} > {h3}:\\n` breadcrumb to every chunk's
+        page_content BEFORE vectorisation.
+
+        The breadcrumb gives the embedding model the section context that
+        a plain mid-section chunk would otherwise lack (e.g. a chunk that
+        contains only "500 THB per night" becomes
+        "Hotel > Hotel Policies & Rules > Pet Policy:\\n500 THB per night").
+        """
+        from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter
+
+        headers_to_split_on = [
+            ("#", "h1"),
+            ("##", "h2"),
+            ("###", "h3"),
+        ]
+        header_splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter(
+            headers_to_split_on=headers_to_split_on,
+            strip_headers=True,
+        )
+        header_chunks = header_splitter.split_text(text)
+
+        out: List[Document] = []
+        for hc in header_chunks:
+            meta = dict(hc.metadata or {})
+            h1 = meta.get("h1", "").strip()
+            h2 = meta.get("h2", "").strip()
+            h3 = meta.get("h3", "").strip()
+            crumb_parts = ["Hotel"]

+            if h2:
+                crumb_parts.append(h2)
+            if h3:

+            breadcrumb = " > ".join(crumb_parts) + ":\n"
+
+            body = hc.page_content.strip()
+            if not body:
+                continue
+
+            base_meta = {**meta, "source": source,
+                         "breadcrumb": breadcrumb.rstrip(":\n")}
+
+            # Fall back to char splitter only if the header chunk is
+            # still too large for the embedding window.
+            if len(body) > self.chunk_size:
+                sub_docs = self.text_splitter.split_documents(
+                    [Document(page_content=body, metadata=base_meta)]
+                )
+                for sd in sub_docs:
+                    sd.page_content = breadcrumb + sd.page_content.strip()
+                    sd.metadata = dict(base_meta)
+                    out.append(sd)
+            else:
+                out.append(Document(page_content=breadcrumb + body,
+                                    metadata=base_meta))

sequencing_notes: Strict apply order: (1) apply the chains.py diff, (2) docker compose restart hotel_guardrails so RERANKER_BACKEND=qwen and the new splitter code both load, (3) run scripts/ingest_hotel_knowledge.py — this is REQUIRED because clear_collection() wipes the 49 existing no-breadcrumb chunks and re-ingests with the new splitter + breadcrumbs. Skipping the re-ingest leaves stale vectors and Phase C delivers zero gain (the reranker would still run, but on header-less chunks). (4) Run the strategic backtest to measure delta. Phase B alone (env var + restart, NO re-ingest) would still work — reranking operates on retrieved Documents regardless of how they were chunked — so if you want to A/B the two phases cleanly: land in two commits — first the RERANKER_BACKEND default flip + docstring (Phase B), restart, run backtest; then the splitter + breadcrumb code (Phase C), re-ingest, run backtest again. The Phase B-only delta should be ~+2 pp; the Phase B+C combined delta ~+6 to +9 pp. Container restart is mandatory because the env var is read at module import time (line 53), not per-request.
